Definition: from G3326 and G1325; to give over, i.e. share:--give, impart.
BiblicalUsage: To share is the plain sense here, and the New Testament makes it practical. John the Baptist tells the man with two coats to give one to the man with none, Paul counts giving among the gifts of grace, and Ephesians tells the reformed thief to work so he has something to give to the needy.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sharing is the test of whether grace has reached our hands: we do not give to earn God's favour, we give because we have received, and the gift counts most when it costs us something we could have kept. That is the shape of grace in the hands: received freely, given freely, and the giving itself is the proof it was received.
